title: Hold a taught word in place
statement: Keep a word being taught in the same place through every stage of its routine, reserving room from the start for any control that appears later.
example: A taught word shifted about 70px sideways when its speaker icon appeared.
detail: A supplied UI review saw a taught word shift about 70px sideways when its speaker icon appeared (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/aladdin-p1-ui-review.reference.md`, line 30). The project found that the 48px speaker was inserted only at the routine's second stage, and reserved its footprint from arrival so the word keeps its position (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/REVIEW-MAPPING.md`, line 15). A rendered fixture verified identical word position and size for all five scoped words at the arrival, sound-out and completed stages (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/STYLE-IMPLEMENTATION-by-residual.md`, line 28).
against: The proof is a component fixture, not the live lesson: "Its screenshot is illustrative component evidence, not an acceptance screenshot of a runtime lesson." (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/STYLE-IMPLEMENTATION-by-residual.md`, line 30).

evidence.quote: Content also moves *within* a screen: on `/p2` the word "betrayal" shifts about 70px sideways when the speaker icon appears, and the forward pill moves down roughly 55px across three steps.
Vocab inserts a48px speaker only atstage2. Reserve its footprint from arrival; retain same word position.

It verifies all five scoped vocabulary words at arrival, sound-out and completed stages: identical word x/y/width/height;48×72 reserve; hidden control before its authored stage;48px target; non-overlapping visible label; visible text contained in its accessible name.
